label: جديد

reel_check.source: yes: Steam store page of GeForce 8800 GTX - 20 Years of a Legend (app 4910040) read in full 6 Nov: free, released 5 Nov 2026, by Dylan Browne, semi-interactive tech demo with DLSS 4.5, path tracing; recommended RTX 4070 and 32 GB RAM; first outlet report 5 Nov evening Dubai; Automaton JP amplified 6 Nov; Publer 7 days and board must_not_repeat clean
reel_check.angle: yes: hook: unbox the GeForce 8800 GTX for free on Steam; why now: released 5 Nov for the card's 20th anniversary; players here: free download, needs a modern RTX card; payoff: the spec line
reel_check.type: yes: OUT NOW: platform Windows via Steam, free (no AED price needed), what it is in one line; the NVIDIA authorisation claim from the digest is NOT on the store page and is left out
reel_check.footage: yes: Steam Launch Trailer (app 4910040), composed locally into live/2026-11-06/gf-frame.mp4 from three clean segments (room and box, the card handled, desk and NVIDIA card), the trailer's own text cards and end slate left out, rows 0 to 1000 kept to clear the trailer's burnt-in tutorial subtitle, centre window 900x1000 at 1.2x in 1080x1200
reel_check.sound: yes: our bed (launch): segments are non-contiguous, so the trailer's sound is not used
reel_check.picture: yes: differs from the last 5 Reels (Tarkov, Psycho-Sleuth, Ocarina scores, Persona 4, Airframe)
reel_check.names: yes: GeForce 8800 GTX, Steam, RTX 4070 Latin; no company or person names on screen
reel_check.not_posted: yes: ledger find recorded in the story file, Publer 7 days checked
reel_check.credit: yes: credit on every clip 0 to 2
reel_check.text_pace: yes: shot 0 headline only, lines on shots 1 and 2, about 3 s of reading in 4 s shots

note: Server lane. Chip جديد: store page read today; the free release was 5 Nov so the post says 'free on Steam', not 'out today'. Picture track composed locally from the Steam launch trailer; our bed. 11.4 s: two facts. v1b: crop rows 0 to 1000 to clear a burnt-in tutorial subtitle seen on the first render's strip; headline keeps the product name as one Latin run so the number order holds.
